🇬🇷 Greece's railways take shape · 1869 → today

Greece's first train ran in 1869, 8 km from Piraeus to Athens. About a third of the network at its peak was built under the Ottoman Empire: Thessaloniki–Idomeni (1872), Thrace (1873), Salonica–Monastir (1894) and Salonica–Constantinople (1896), all inherited after 1912–1920. The network peaked at around 2,550 km in the 1950s. Then the debt crisis hit: the whole metre-gauge Peloponnese network has had its services suspended since 2011, and Storm Daniel shut Thessaly's lines in 2023. Suspended lines are shown as closed; the line that became Athens Metro line 1 stays drawn.

📊 Data: opening and closure year of every section, sourced line by line (greekrailtickets.gr, Wikipedia, Hellenic Parliament); track geometry © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL). A few dates differ by a year between sources.
